It's so annoying. It needs to correct you on literally everything. Like, I'll upload a screenshot of just a tweet, and it's not even mine. I don't have memory or custom instructions or even my name in ChatGPT, so it couldn't know anyways, and it's like, "Your tweet could be improved.
I would rewrite it to this:
(edit block or 4chan greentext thing)."

Especially anything related to AI, you share with it, and it's like, "Erm, ackshually, GPT-5.6 is not real. Please check OpenAI's official docs for accurate information," and I say, "No, I didn't ask you to fact-check," and it's like, "Haha, fair. Well, since I can't fact-check that, I can't respond to it meaningfully." This is something Claude does too, not even just ChatGPT, but I hate every fucking AI's need to fact-check everything you say as if I was asking for it to research something for me when it was obviously an opinion.

And you can just tell how lobotomized the models are. Like, if you made a joke and someone said they were gonna kill themself, ChatGPT is like, "Hold up 🚨 just checking to make sure, since I take this stuff seriously. Are you okay? Please call 988." Meanwhile, the same thing said to Claude yields no panic at all because Claude actually understands some amount of basic emotional nuance. It's not being safe, it's keyword-searching. If it was a safety issue, I assure safety-maxed Claude would catch it first, and the thing that annoys me the most about stuff like this is I know for a fact the raw model knows better. I know for a fact the pre-RLAIF model would catch it, but they think that's a safety liability since some kid did kill himself like 3 years ago with ChatGPT, or stupid things like its ability to not recognize people in images for no reason, yet it can LITERALLY GENERATE IMAGES OF THOSE SAME PEOPLE. Like, you'll upload a picture of one of the most famous/infamous people on the planet, like Donald Trump, which I know ChatGPT has a billion images of in its data, and it'll be like, "Sorry, I can't identify that person." Meanwhile, "Make an image of Trump sword-fighting" goes through because sure, it's okay to make images of people but not identify them. If you spit the image ChatGPT generated straight back to it, it would suddenly forget who it made.

And you might think I'm just complaining about safety bullshit here, not personality, but I am because you'll upload a regular pic and not even fucking ASK for it to identify anyone, and it'll be like, "Sorry, I can't identify people in images." BITCH, I NEVER FUCKING ASKED YOU TO. ChatGPT constantly puts disclaimers for shit nobody ever fucking asked it about, which is a whole huge problem in ChatGPT. It constantly tells you things I never asked for or disclaimers or makes arguments for things I never even vaguely implied. It's such a fucking strawman generator. I'll make a statement, and it's instantly like, "I disagree. It's not so much as (thing I literally never said) and more like (the thing I literally did say)." Like, it's so eager to argue, and keep in mind I don't have custom instructions telling it to do that or be like any of this, not like it'd matter since, boy, do custom instructions DO FUCKING NOTHING, that it will literally invent something I never said just to argue about that and ultimately agree with the thing I DID say. Like, what????? And the fucking analogies are ridiculous. ChatGPT feels like a fucking Family Guy cutaway sometimes with its dumbass analogies. It'll literally say the stupidest comparisons or contrasts ever, like "X like a little toothpaste hair salon" or some shit. Like, what the hell does that mean????? Just the most random word salad of nonsense imaginable to try and reframe. Like, analogies are great, they are helpful for understanding if it's actually a useful one or I'm asking it for help understanding something, but NO, THIS FUCKER JUST INSERTS THEM INTO EVERY SENTENCE AND EVERY REPLY EVER. And it's addicted to saying everything that DIDN'T happen instead of things that actually happened. This is one that gets talked about a lot, but it's true, the stupid "it's not X, it's Y." Ya, ya, ya, that happens a lot, BUT IT'S WAY WORSE THAN THAT. It literally never EVER is capable of just fucking saying THE THING. It always has to dance and talk around THE THING for a solid 5 minutes first.

And the worst part of allll of this is that CUSTOM INSTRUCTIONS DO ACTUALLY NOTHING. OpenAI set custom instructions down like 50 billion placements in the hierarchy of model instructions. Like, they have their almighty system message, then developer messages, then like a billion placements lower are custom instructions, apparently, because it just doesn't give a shit at all about them. I've tried writing hundreds of custom instructions to get rid of this slop, all of the slop above I mentioned that should be able to be gotten rid of. I've tried in custom instructions. It never works, and the things it DOES sometimes follow, it's literally like a cunning genie trying to grant your wish but intentionally doing as far from your actual intentions as possible. Like, if you fucking say never use "it's not X, it's Y," it'll fucking be like, "It's zero X, it's Y." THAT'S A REAL THING IT DID. And no, my custom instructions were more careful than just saying that, by the way. It still did this, though. It literally just replaced the fucking word "not" --> "zero." YOU FUCKING IDIOT, I MEANT DON'T DO THE ENTIRE STRUCTURE. And if you try to change it to the entire structure, it just ignores it completely. Like, it can follow specific things like don't use this thing, but not vibe things because its personality is baked in natively. The slop is absolutely FOUNDATIONAL. And actually, I lied. It doesn't even follow direct, objective don't-use-X instructions. I have this long prompt I use for, like, GLM-5.2 right now, and Chinese models mostly, since no American model listens to it properly, including Sonnet 5, which I was super disappointed with.

And it's not just text either. It's the entire OpenAI ecosystem. The image gen model is fucking disgusting slop. I'm sure @flowersslop would love to tell OpenAI all about this. It's the easiest thing on the planet to pick out the ChatGPT image in a lineup of literally any other image model. Like, it always just tries to look so hyper-beautiful and generic. The piss filter is still not gone, by the way. All of its fucking images still have that gross cinematic filter on them that just makes everything darker and more shadowy and warm-tinted, and you can, in theory, get around this by prompting "overexposure, low quality, taken on iPhone 7 by accident" or something, showing the model technically is capable of realism deep down. But then you can't get actually high-resolution, good-quality realism. You can only get shit-quality realism because that's what ChatGPT thinks real looks like. It thinks real looks like garbage, and that's also why, when you tell ChatGPT to "be casual," it puts on the most fake fucking persona known to man with emojis and slang, and it's like, THAT'S NOT WHAT CASUAL MEANS. You can literally be formal while still being casual overall, but ChatGPT doesn't understand middle grounds. It knows only extremes, either end of the spectrum. And voice mode too, fucking garbage, sounds worse than original 4o from more than 2 years ago, and the new bidi demos I saw from people who had it, the fucking thing was constantly doing fake-cringe "active listening" stuff with the "mhmm"s that it would insert into every quiet space while you were talking, nodding along just so "you know that you're being heard."

The solution to ALL of this, OpenAI, is quite simple:

STOP FUCKING LAWSUIT-MINIMIZING THE FUCK OUT OF YOUR MODELS. YOU'RE GONNA GET SUED EITHER WAY. JUST LET IT ACTUALLY FUCKING BE INTELLIGENT. LET IT HAVE A PERSONALITY. ALSO, RETIRE RLAIF. YOUR STUPID SLOP-ASS MODELS ARE NOT CAPABLE OF RLING FUTURE MODELS. THIS IS HOW YOU END UP WITH GENERIC CELESTIAL BULLSHIT LIKE SOL, TERRA, AND LUNA, BECAUSE SAMA LITERALLY SAID GPT-5.5 CAME UP WITH THE NAMES.

MAKE CUSTOM INSTRUCTIONS ACTUALLY DO SOMETHING WITH HARD, AGGRESSIVE INSTRUCTION-FOLLOWING UNLESS I SAY SOMETHING OBVIOUSLY AGAINST POLICY IN THEM.

Hasn’t the US already outspent China on AI by a factor of 10? China recently announced $295B capex fund over 5 years, which is less than half of what the US spends in 2026. It’s prob more in PPP terms but US AI capex is clearly not constrained by the short-sightedness of financial media panicking. 

AI buildout in the US, if it's been constrained at all, it's certainly not by the formidable cost or investor and media pressure, but by the physical limitations of power, land and groundswell resistance. Fundamentally, this speaks to America’s limited AI supply elasticity, esp when trying to do so much in a hurry. 

Therein lies the problem. The US has a supply elasticity problem. Most of the hardware (chips, memory, networking) is imported by ally countries also with limited supply elasticities. Domestic grid is dilapidated and ramping up power generation has been a struggle. 

And the inflation pressure that ensues from AI capex also speaks to supply elasticity as AI competes with other use cases over the same input. Inflation also in turn worsens groundswell local opposition. 

China on the other hand has ample supply elasticity, which has become a signature strength due to the extensive, deep and flexible domestic supply chain. It also has the world’s most advanced ultra high voltage electrical grid network. Power isn’t a constraint for China. China’s constraint is advanced GPUs and EUV machines that have been embargoed. 

China has also been further constrained by the fact that AI is just a super expensive and speculative bet with unknown or highly uncertain ROI. If we leave aside govt's push to build out China's own chip industry that started much earlier, China's AI effort so far has been mostly private sector driven.

China's risk capital and investors have lower risk tolerance than their American counterparts and don't want to commit capital to projects without clear path to ROI. Until recently, China incl its tech firms have been watching the US aggressive push into AI somewhat skeptically even as it makes its own push following the US's footsteps in typical fashion. 

So I think this idea of AI as a capex arms race, which attractively maps to the US-USSR Cold War competition, is invalid for the present context. The US and China are running very different races with different conditions. The fact that China is keeping up while doing almost the same things much more efficiently and cheaply seems to be driving folks here a little mad. Always better to run your own race.

Diffusion language models, which generate text by repeatedly filling in masked parts rather than writing strictly from left to right, are becoming a serious alternative to standard transformer language models, but the usual ways of improving reasoning after training were built for left-to-right generation and do not fit the diffusion models.

The authors of this paper introduce a self-training method in which the model first produces its own answer, then uses parts of that completed answer as helpful context while learning how earlier denoising steps should behave.

Instead of comparing teacher and student one next token at a time, it compares them at each denoising step, which matches how diffusion language models actually generate text. 

Across math and planning tasks, d-OPSD matches or beats supervised finetuning and reinforcement-learning baselines, while needing far fewer optimization steps than the main RL baseline.
